Rashi on Chullin 23a:1:1.hebrew: למעוטי נרבע ונעבד - ואף על גב דתנא קתני "פרט לתחלת הציהוב", אסמכתא בעלמא הוא, ולעולם פסולייהו משום ספיקא. רובע ליכא למימר בעופות, דאין לך עוף רובע:
Rashi on Chullin 23a:1:1.english: To exclude an animal that was the passive partner in bestiality, and one that was worshiped - And although the tanna taught, "This excludes the beginning of yellowing," that is merely an asmakhta (a textual hook for a rabbinic law), and in truth their disqualification is because of doubt. It is not possible to say [the case of] one that engaged in bestiality with regard to birds, since there is no bird that is the active partner in bestiality.

Rashi on Chullin 23a:2:1.english: Since it is written - Regarding offerings:

Rashi on Chullin 23a:2:2.hebrew: כי משחתם בהם מום בם - לא ירצו לכם, דבין השחתה בין מום פוסלים בהם. ותנא דבי רבי ישמעאל וכו':
Rashi on Chullin 23a:2:2.english: For their corruption is in them, a blemish is in them - "They shall not be accepted for you" [Leviticus 22:25], as both corruption and a blemish disqualify them. And the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught, etc.

Rashi on Chullin 23a:2:3.english: A matter of illicit relations - [An animal that] mounts or is mounted [in a forbidden act].

Rashi on Chullin 23a:2:4.english: Idolatry - [The case of an animal] that was worshiped, where [its owner] bowed down to his animal.

Rashi on Chullin 23a:2:5.hebrew: כי השחית כל בשר - בדור המבול כתיב, ודור המבול בערוה קלקלו, כדכתיב (בראשית ו) ויקחו להם נשים וגו', שהיו נזקקין לנשי ריעיהן ולכל בהמה וחיה:
Rashi on Chullin 23a:2:5.english: For all flesh had corrupted - This is written regarding the generation of the Flood, and the generation of the Flood corrupted [their way] through illicit relations, as it is written (Genesis 6) "And they took for themselves wives," etc., for they would have relations with the wives of their fellows and with every animal and beast.

Rashi on Chullin 23a:3:1.hebrew: בבהמה - כתיב "תמים זכר", אבל עוף לא כתיב ביה לא "תמים" ולא "זכר". הלכך לא פסלי בהו מומין קטנים, כגון דוקין שבעין, אלא מומין גדולים, כגון מחוסר אבר, משום "הקריבהו נא לפחתך":
Rashi on Chullin 23a:3:1.english: In the case of an animal - It is written "unblemished, male," but with regard to a bird, neither "unblemished" nor "male" is written about it. Therefore minor blemishes do not disqualify them, such as specks in the eye, but only major blemishes, such as a missing limb, because of [the verse] "Offer it now to your governor."

Rashi on Chullin 23a:4:1.hebrew: מן האיל או מן הכבש - מאיזה שארצה:
Rashi on Chullin 23a:4:1.english: From the ram or from the lamb - Whichever I wish.

Rashi on Chullin 23a:4:2.hebrew: פלגס - כבש בן שנה בתוך שנתו קרוי כבש, ואיל משעברו י"ג חדשים, שנכנס חדש שלם בתוך שנה שניה, קרוי איל עד עולם. פלגס בתוך חדש ראשון של שנה שניה:
Rashi on Chullin 23a:4:2.english: Palgas - A lamb within its first year is called a lamb (*kevess*). And once thirteen months have passed, meaning that a full month has entered into the second year, it is called a ram (*ayil*) forever. A *palgas* is [an animal] within the first month of the second year.

Rashi on Chullin 23a:5:1.hebrew: הקריבו - משנה היא במסכת פרה (פ"א מ"ג), ובפלגס קא מיירי:
Rashi on Chullin 23a:5:1.english: They offered - This is a mishna in tractate Parah (chapter 1, mishna 3), and it is speaking of a pelges.

Rashi on Chullin 23a:5:2.hebrew: ואין עולה לו מזבחו - אם היה מחוייב איל לבדו או כבש לבדו, וטעמא לא מפרש תנא, אי משום ספיקא אי משום בריה:
Rashi on Chullin 23a:5:2.english: And his altar-offering does not count for him - If he was obligated to bring a ram alone or a lamb alone. And the tanna does not explain the reason, whether it is because of uncertainty or because of [the principle that the offering] is a new creation.

Rashi on Chullin 23a:6:1.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said - From where do we know that he brings for it the libations of a ram, two tenth-measures [of flour] and a third of a hin of wine? For it is written in the section on libations, in [the passage of] "Send for yourself men": "Or for the one ram, etc." – "or" [comes] to include the pelagas in these libations. And since the verse was needed to include [it], we may conclude that Rabbi Yochanan holds like the first Tanna, who said that its altar-offering does not count for him, because it is a creature in its own right, and that the Merciful One included it with regard to libations. For if it were a case of uncertainty, the verse would not include it, since, as it may be a ram, it is obvious that he must bring the libations of a ram. And [it is] stipulated that if it is a ram, they will be his own, and if it is a lamb, they will be a permitted voluntary offering, for one may donate libations without an animal offering, as we say in Menachot, in the last chapter (107a). And even though it was taught that one may not donate one log, nor two, nor five, but [only] three, so that they are called the libations of a lamb, or four, so that they are called the libations of a ram, or six, which are fit for a bull - here, in a case like this, it is [brought] together with other offerings.

Tosafot on Chullin 23a:1:1.hebrew: כי איצטריך קרא למעוטי נרבע ונעבד - תימה, דסותר סתמא דש"ס דרשא דברייתא כדי לדחות ראייתו, ומוקי ליה קרא לדרשא אחרת. ויש לומר דקים ליה דאצטריך קרא להאי דרשא, דהא רבי עקיבא אית ליה דרשא דמשחתם בפרק בתרא דבכורות (דף נז.), דקסבר מעשר בהמה חל על רובע ונרבע כמו שחל על בעלי מומין. ומשמע בפרק המזבח מקדש (זבחים דף פה:) דאית ליה נרבע בעופות, דקאמר רבי עקיבא מכשיר בעלי מומין ולא קאמר ובנרבע, הואיל וכשר בעופות; ומנא ליה, אלא ע"כ מהאי קרא. וא"ת א"כ תפשוט דספיקא הוי, דאי בריה הוי אצטריך קרא למעוטי, וא"כ מנלן דיש נרבע בעופות. ונ"ל דמעיקרא ס"ד ודאי דאיצטריך קרא למעוטי אי הוה בריה, אבל השתא דמסיק דאצטריך קרא לנרבע ונעבד, ס"ל דלבריה לא אצטריך קרא למעוטי, דממילא אימעיט מבתורים דומיא דבני יונה; מה בני יונה דוקא קטנים, אף תורים דוקא גדולים, למעוטי תחלת הציהוב שבזה ושבזה דלא הוי לא קטנים ולא גדולים. ודרשא דברייתא אסמכתא בעלמא היא. ומורי ה"ר אהרן מריגנשפור"ק תירץ דאינו סותר השתא דרשא דברייתא, דתרי מיעוטי כתיבי, מן התורים או מן בני היונה: חד למעוטי נרבע ונעבד ולאפוקי מדרשא דמשחתם, ואידך למעוטי תחלת הציהוב. וקמי שמיא ודאי גליא אי קטנים הוו אי גדולים הוו, ואי קטנים הוו ממעטינהו מן התורים, ואי גדולים הוו ממעטינהו מבני היונה, ואנן הוא דלא ידעינן מהי ממעטינהו. והשתא אי בריה הוו אתי נמי שפיר, כמו שפירש לפי המסקנא, דחד למעוטי בריה וחד למעוטי נרבע ונעבד; ומעיקרא ס"ד דאצטריך תרוייהו לבריה, דאי לא הוה כתיב אלא חד מיעוטא לא הוה ממעטי להו אלא או מגדולים או מקטנים, ואם הביא משניהם הוה נפיק ממה נפשך. אבל ק"ק על פירושו, דאי אתא קרא לאשמועינן שהם או גדולים או קטנים, אף ע"ג דקמי שמיא גליא, א"כ מאי פריך בסוף על אלו מומין שהבאתי לעיל, מני? אילימא ת"ק, ספק הוא, איצטריך קרא למעוטי ספיקא; נימא דקרא מיעט לאנדרוגינוס או משום שהוא זכר משונה או משום דאשמעינן שהוא נקבה, ואנן הוא דלא ידעינן הוי ספק? אלא משמע אם קמי שמיא גליא שהוא נקבה לא היה לו להשמיענו. והא דאיכא תרי מיעוטי, איכא למימר דאתא חד לנרבע וחד לנעבד. ויותר נראה דנרבע ונעבד נפקי מחד מיעוטא, אלא אצטריך חד מיעוטא לתורים וחד לבני יונה; ולמאי דס"ד נמי מעיקרא דאתא למעוטי בריה, אצטריך תרי מיעוטי, חד למעוטי תורים וחד לבני יונה:
Tosafot on Chullin 23a:1:1.english: When the verse was needed to exclude an animal that was mounted (nirva) or worshipped (ne'evad) - It is astonishing: [the Gemara] contradicts the standard [understanding] of the Talmud, [namely] the derivation of the baraita, in order to refute [Rav Pappa's] proof, and it establishes the verse as [coming for] a different derivation! And one may say that [the Gemara] holds that the verse is needed for this derivation, for Rabbi Akiva has the derivation of "mishchatam" in the last chapter of Bekhorot (57a), as he holds that animal tithe applies to one that was mounted (rove'a) or one that was the object of bestiality (nirva'), just as it applies to blemished animals. And it is implied in the chapter [Ha-Mizbe'ach Mekadesh] (Zevachim 85b) that he holds there is [the disqualification of] nirva among birds, for Rabbi Akiva says that [the altar] renders blemished animals valid, and does not say "and one that was the object of bestiality (nirva)," since it is valid among birds. And from where does he derive this? Rather, it must be from this verse. And if you say: if so, resolve [the question] that it is a doubt, for if it were a distinct creature (beriyah), the verse was needed to exclude [it], and if so, from where do we know that there is nirva among birds? But it seems to me that at first it was thought that certainly the verse was needed to exclude [it] if it were a distinct creature, but now that [the Gemara] concludes that the verse was needed for nirva and ne'evad, it holds that for a distinct creature the verse was not needed to exclude [it], since it is excluded automatically from "turtledoves" (torim), by comparison to "young pigeons" (benei yonah): just as young pigeons [must be] specifically small, so turtledoves [must be] specifically grown, to exclude the first stage of yellowing [of the plumage] in both of these, which is neither small nor grown. And the derivation of the baraita is merely an asmakhta (a rabbinic law loosely supported by a verse). And my teacher, R. Aharon of Regensburg, answered that [the Gemara] now does not contradict the derivation of the baraita, for two exclusions are written, "from the turtledoves or from the young pigeons": one to exclude nirva and ne'evad, and to remove [the case] from the derivation of "mishchatam," and the other to exclude the first stage of yellowing. And before Heaven it is certainly revealed whether they were small or whether they were grown; if they were small, they are excluded from the turtledoves, and if they were grown, they are excluded from the young pigeons, and it is we who do not know from which they are excluded. And now, if it were a distinct creature (beriyah), this also works well, as [Rashi] explained according to the conclusion, that one [exclusion] is to exclude a distinct creature and one to exclude nirva and ne'evad; and at first it was thought that both were needed for a distinct creature, for if only one exclusion were written, it would exclude them only from grown ones or from small ones, and if one brought [birds] of both, he would fulfill [his obligation] in any case. But I have difficulty with his explanation, for if the verse comes to teach us that they are either grown or small, even though it is revealed before Heaven, then what does [the Gemara] ask at the end about these blemishes that I brought above: "Who is [the author]? If you say it is the first Tanna, it is a doubt; was a verse needed to exclude a doubt?" Let us say that the verse excluded an androgynos, either because it is an unusual male or because it teaches us that it is female, and it is we who do not know, so it is a doubt! Rather, it implies that if it is revealed before Heaven that it is female, [the verse] should not have taught it to us. And as for the fact that there are two exclusions, one can say that one comes for nirva and one for ne'evad. But it seems more likely that nirva and ne'evad derive from one exclusion, but one exclusion is needed for turtledoves and one for young pigeons; and according to what was thought at first as well, that it comes to exclude a distinct creature, two exclusions were needed, one to exclude turtledoves and one for young pigeons:

Tosafot on Chullin 23a:2:1.hebrew: כי משחתם בהם מום בם - כאן משמע דלכ"ע אית להו הך דרשא דמשחתם, דאי פליג אדרשא זו ההוא תנא דדריש מן הבהמה להוציא את הרובע, אם כן לידוק דבריה הוי למאן דלא דריש דרשא דמשחתם. אלא ודאי כולהו דרשי להו, ואפילו הכי איצטריך מן הבהמה ומן הבקר להוציא רובע ונרבע, ולא הוי דרשינן ממשחתם, דהא בהא תליא, אלא משום דאשכחן כבר בקדשים ששוים בהן דבר ערוה ועבודת כוכבים ומום, ונ"מ דרשא דמשחתם למעשר בהמה דחל על רובע ונרבע כמו שחל על בעל מום. (ולרבי ישמעאל) [ולר"ש] נ"מ גם לפרה. וא"ת, בריש כל האסורין (תמורה דף כח:) אמרינן דתנא דמשחתם מוקי קרא דמן הבהמה פרט לזקן וחולה ומזוהם. ויש לומר, דתנא דמשחתם ודאי משמע ליה לש"ס דמפיק רובע ונרבע ממשחתם לחודיה, אבל שאר תנאי דנפקי ממן הבהמה אית להו דרשא דמשחתם כדפרישית. וכן משמע בפרק בתרא דבכורות (דף נז.) דפליגי התם כמה תנאי גבי מעשר בהמה, גבי טומטום ואנדרוגינוס ובמחוסר זמן ויוצא דופן, אבל בנרבע ורובע ומוקצה ונעבד לא אשכחן שום פלוגתא, ומשמע דכולהו מודו דמתעשרין, כדדרשינן התם ממשחתם. ומיהו מהכא איכא למדחי, דאפילו מאן דלית ליה דרשא דמשחתם איצטריך מן התורים למעוטי נרבע, דסלקא דעתך כיון דעופות ליתנהו ברובע ליתנהו נמי בנרבע, דכה"ג אמר בפרק המזבח מקדש (זבחים פה:):
Tosafot on Chullin 23a:2:1.english: "For their corruption is in them, a blemish is in them" - Here it implies that according to everyone, they hold this derivation of "mishchatam" ("their corruption"). For if that Tanna who expounds "from the animal" to exclude the rove'a (one that mounted) disagreed with this derivation, then his statement would have to be understood as [being in accordance with] the one who does not expound the derivation of "mishchatam". Rather, certainly all of them expound it, and even so "from the animal" and "from the cattle" were needed to exclude one that mounted (rove'a) and one that was mounted (nirba), and we would not have derived it from "mishchatam", for the one depends on the other; rather, [they were needed] because we already find in sacrifices that a sexual transgression, idolatry, and a blemish are equated in them. And the practical difference of the derivation of "mishchatam" is for animal tithe, which takes effect on a rove'a and a nirba just as it takes effect on a blemished animal. (And according to R. Yishmael) [And according to R. Shimon] there is a practical difference also for the red heifer. And if you ask: In the beginning of the chapter "Kol ha-Asurin" (Temurah 28b) we say that the Tanna of "mishchatam" establishes the verse "from the animal" to exclude an old, sick, or filthy (mezuham) [animal]. And one can say that regarding the Tanna of "mishchatam", the Talmud certainly understands that he derives rove'a and nirba from "mishchatam" alone, but the other Tannaim who derive [exclusions] from "from the animal" hold the derivation of "mishchatam" as I explained. And so it implies in the last chapter of Bekhorot (57a), where several Tannaim disagree there regarding animal tithe, concerning a tumtum and an androgynos, and one lacking [the requisite] time, and one born by caesarean section (yotzei dofen); but regarding a nirba and a rove'a, and a muktzeh and a ne'evad, we do not find any dispute, and it implies that all agree that they are tithed, as we expound there from "mishchatam". However, from here [the opposing view] can be pushed aside, [for] even one who does not hold the derivation of "mishchatam" needed [the verse] "from the turtledoves" to exclude a nirba, for you might have thought that since birds are not subject to [the law of] rove'a, they are also not subject to [the law of] nirba, as it says in a similar manner in the chapter "ha-Mizbe'ach Mekadesh" (Zevachim 85b):

Tosafot on Chullin 23a:3:1.hebrew: תמות וזכרות בבהמה - בת"כ דריש לה מדכתיב "תמים זכר בבקר בכשבים ובעזים": תמות וזכרות בבהמה, ואין תמות וזכרות בעופות. ומחוסר אבר דפסול בעוף, נפקא ליה מדכתיב "מן העוף" ולא כל העוף, בפ"ק דקדושין (דף כד:); ולא כמו שפירש כאן בקונטרס משום "הקריבהו נא לפחתך". וא"ת, ל"ל קרא לפסול מחוסר אבר, והא אפילו לבני נח נמי אסור, דליכא מידי דלישראל שרי ולבני נח אסור? וי"ל, משום דאמרינן בפרק ארבע מיתות (סנהדרין דף נט.) דכל מצוה שנאמרה לבני נח ולא נשנית בסיני, לישראל נאמרה ולא לבני נח; ולכך הוצרך לשנותה, כדי לאסור לזה ולזה. וא"ת, ל"ל קרא דאין תמות וזכרות בעופות? מדאצטריך "מן העוף" לאסור מחוסר אבר, ידעינן דאין מום פוסל בעוף, דאי פוסל, למה לי "מן העוף"? ויש לומר, דאי לאו קרא דאין תמות וזכרות בעופות, ה"א דמום פוסל בעוף, ו"מן העוף" אתא לאסור אפילו הנך מומין דשרו בבהמה, דקרא דמן העוף לאסור אתא ולא להתיר. ואין להקשות נמי, מדאיצטריך "מן התורים" לנרבע ונעבד, שמעינן שפיר דאין מום פוסל בעופות; דאיכא למימר דאיצטריך "מן התורים" משום דסלקא דעתין, כיון דעופות ליתנהו ברובע, ליתנהו נמי בנרבע, כדפרישית לעיל:
Tosafot on Chullin 23a:3:1.english: Wholeness and maleness apply to an animal - In the Torat Kohanim, [the Tanna] derives it from what is written, "a male without blemish, from the cattle, from the sheep, or from the goats": wholeness and maleness apply to an animal, but wholeness and maleness do not apply to birds. And [the rule] that a bird lacking a limb is disqualified is derived from what is written, "from the birds" and not all the birds, in the first chapter of Kiddushin (24b); and not as Rashi explained here, on account of "present it now to your governor" (Malachi 1:8). And if you ask: Why is a verse needed to disqualify one lacking a limb? Surely it is forbidden even to the Noahides, for there is nothing that is permitted to Israel and forbidden to the Noahides! And one can answer: Because we say in the chapter "Arba Mitot" (Sanhedrin 59a) that any commandment that was stated to the Noahides and was not repeated at Sinai to Israel, was stated to Israel and not to the Noahides; and therefore it was necessary to repeat it, in order to forbid it to this one and to that one. And if you ask: Why is a verse needed for [the rule] that wholeness and maleness do not apply to birds? Since "from the birds" was needed to forbid one lacking a limb, we know that a blemish does not disqualify a bird, for if it did disqualify, why do I need "from the birds"? And one can say: Were it not for the verse that wholeness and maleness do not apply to birds, I would have thought that a blemish disqualifies a bird, and "from the birds" came to forbid even those blemishes that are permitted in an animal, for the verse "from the birds" came to forbid and not to permit. Nor should one object further: Since "from the turtledoves" was needed for an animal that was the object of bestiality (nirba') or that was worshipped (ne'evad), we surely learn that a blemish does not disqualify birds. For one can say that "from the turtledoves" was needed because it would have entered our mind that since birds do not apply to a robe'a (one who commits bestiality), they also do not apply to a nirba', as I explained above:

Tosafot on Chullin 23a:7:1.hebrew: כי תבעי לך אליבא דבר פדא - בפ' שתי מדות (מנחות דף צא:) איתותב בר פדא מהאי קרא דאו לאיל, דמדרבה פלגס, דלא אתא קרא לרבויי ספיקא:
Tosafot on Chullin 23a:7:1.english: When you should raise the question, it is according to Bar Pada - In the chapter Shetei Middot (Menachot 91b), Bar Pada was refuted from this verse, "or for a ram" (Numbers 15:6), for [the Torah] divided the ram from the [other] offerings by expanding [its measure], since the verse did not come to include a case of doubt.
